newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS SEES MORE JOB CUTS IN RESTRUCTURE.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS SEES MORE JOB CUTS IN RESTRUCTURE.

text.p: Philips Electronics, announcing a one billion guilder charge for the current fourth quarter, said on Thursday that net job cuts were on the way as it restructured its underperforming units.
"There will be a loss of jobs and a gaining of jobs," finance director Dudley Eustace told a news conference.
"There will be a loss of jobs in those areas which are high cost and a gaining of jobs in those geographical areas which offer lower cost labour," he said.
"It's a fair guess to say more jobs will be lost than gained in western Europe."

All sectors of the company would be looked at, although the Sound & Vision unit had already had an 800 million guilder gross provision made at the second quarter, and 75 percent-owned music and movies unit PolyGram announced a $90 million restructuring charge on Wednesday.
"Sound & Vision was looked after at the end of June. The one billion (guilder charge) covers pretty well all other divisions, including PolyGram and including lighting."
"Those businesses which are losing money or not making the grade will be either sold or closed down depending on what the market's prepared to pay," said Eustace.
"We're leaving no business unexamined for the possibility to optimise shareholder value," he added.

A net 6,000 jobs were expected to go at Sound & Vision, covered by the 800 million guilder gross charge, but Eustace declined to say whether the billion guilder charge meant a similar number of jobs would be cut elsewhere.

"It will be an ongoing process through 1997. Will it all be complete by the end of 1997?...that depends very much on the market. I would hope that the bulk of these measures will have been completed by the end of next year," Eustace told reporters. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
